title: The last bytes of a file
summary: tail -c with lseek: jump near the end and copy from there with read and write.
hints: `lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END)` returns the size of the file. The place to start is `size - n`, or 0 if the file is smaller than `n`.
Then `lseek(fd, start, SEEK_SET)` and a `read`/`write` loop with a buffer, until `read` returns 0. The file may contain 0 bytes: never use `printf` or string functions.
